title: Indian Polity & Constitution
intro: Polity is the most scoring GA topic because it is rule-based, not event-based: the Constitution says exactly one thing, and SSC asks exactly that. Master the structure — the Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Duties, the Directive Principles, and the three organs (legislature, executive, judiciary) — and tie key facts to article numbers. Once you know that Article 14 is equality and Article 21 is life and liberty, those marks are automatic.

topics.name: The Constitution & Its Making
topics.details: The Constituent Assembly drafted the Constitution; Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'. It was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.

solved.problem: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
When was the Constitution adopted, and when did it come into force?
From which country did India borrow Fundamental Rights?
Which amendment added "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble?

unsolved.problem: Who is called the Father of the Indian Constitution?
Constitution Day is observed on?
The Directive Principles were borrowed from?
The parliamentary system was adopted from?
The Constitution came into force in which year?

topics.name: Fundamental Rights & Duties
topics.details: The six Fundamental Rights (Articles 12–35) are guaranteed to citizens; Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) is the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

solved.problem: Which article guarantees the Right to Equality?
Which article protects the Right to Life and Personal Liberty?
Which right did Ambedkar call the "heart and soul" of the Constitution?
Fundamental Duties are listed in which article?

unsolved.problem: How many Fundamental Rights are there today?
Right to Life and Liberty is under which article?
Fundamental Duties were added by which amendment?
The Right to ___ was removed as a Fundamental Right in 1978.
Article 32 provides the Right to?

topics.name: Parliament & Executive
topics.details: Parliament has two Houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). The President (Article 52) is the constitutional head; real executive power rests with the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 75).

solved.problem: Which House is called the House of the People?
Who is the constitutional head of the Indian State?
In which House can a Money Bill be introduced?
Who holds real executive power in India?
solved.solution: The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

topics.name: Judiciary & Constitutional Bodies
topics.details: The Supreme Court (Article 124) is the apex court and guardian of the Constitution; High Courts head the judiciary in the states. Independent constitutional bodies include the Election Commission, CAG, UPSC and the Finance Commission.

solved.problem: Which article establishes the Supreme Court of India?
Which body conducts elections in India?
What is the retirement age of a Supreme Court judge?
Who audits the accounts of the Union and States?
solved.solution: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG, Article 148).

shortcuts: Tie every fact to an article number — SSC asks the exact article.
Article 14 = Equality, 21 = Life & Liberty, 32 = Constitutional Remedies.
42nd Amendment (1976) = Duties + Socialist/Secular; 44th (1978) removed Right to Property.
Money Bill only in Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha is permanent.
mistakes: Mixing the adoption date (26 Nov 1949) with the enforcement date (26 Jan 1950).
Counting seven Fundamental Rights — Property was removed in 1978 (now six).
Confusing which amendment added Duties (42nd) vs removed Property (44th).
Swapping SC (65) and HC (62) retirement ages.
pyq: SSC Tier 1 loves article-number questions (14, 21, 32, 51A, 324), the Houses of Parliament, and amendment facts (42nd, 44th). Direct, rule-based recall makes Polity the most scoring GA topic.
summary: Polity rewards article-anchored recall. Know the Preamble, the six Fundamental Rights (Art 14, 21, 32), Directive Principles, and Duties (51A, 42nd Amendment); the two Houses and the President–PM executive; and the apex court plus constitutional bodies (EC 324, CAG 148, UPSC 315). Exact article numbers win the marks.
